inclusion.I2: Human participants performing an emotion regulation or reappraisal task, broadly defined. Reappraisal covers a wide spectrum of tactics including reinterpretation, perspective-taking, and distancing.
inclusion.I3: Includes at least one group of healthy adults. A study of a patient population qualifies if it also includes a healthy control group.

exclusion.E1: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses) without original human data.
exclusion.E2: Doesn't include at least one healthy adult sample.
exclusion.E3: The abstract clearly indicates that the emotional stimuli being regulated are something other than static pictures - e.g. film or video clips, music or other audio, odours, narrative scripts, recalled autobiographical memories, imagined scenarios, monetary or social decision outcomes, or delivered pain. Apply this only when the abstract states the stimulus type; if the stimulus type is not stated, do NOT exclude on this basis.

inclusion.I6: fMRI Task- reappraisal used as the emotion regulation strategy, construed broadly to include reinterpretation, perspective-taking, and distancing tactics. The regulation goal may be up-regulation (increase) OR down-regulation (decrease) of emotion, and the emotional stimuli may be positive OR negative. A study qualifies if it implements EITHER regulation direction with EITHER stimulus valence; it does NOT need to include both directions or both valences.
inclusion.I7: Stimuli- the emotional stimuli being regulated are static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures, photographs of faces or scenes). Exclude studies in which the regulated stimuli are film or video clips, audio, narrative scripts, imagined or recalled autobiographical scenarios, monetary or social decision outcomes, anticipatory cues, or delivered pain/shock.
inclusion.I8: Target sample- at least one group of healthy adults with no prior report of neurological, medical, or psychiatric disorders. A study of a patient or clinical population qualifies only if results for the healthy control group are reported separately; only that group is of interest.
inclusion.I9: Analysis- Reports at least one within-task contrast related to emotion regulation (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”, “up-regulate > maintain”) for the target sample.
inclusion.I10: Whole-brain evidence- The target analysis must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map, with peak coordinates reported in a standard anatomical reference space (Talairach/Tournoux or MNI).
inclusion.I11: Verifiability- the qualifying whole-brain coordinates must be present in the text you have been given: a table of peak coordinates, or coordinates quoted in the Results narrative. Coordinates in tables, figures, or supplementary materials qualify only if their actual values appear in the provided text. A citation to a supplementary table, appendix, or online resource whose contents are NOT in the provided text does not satisfy this criterion.

exclusion.E4: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original fMRI data in healthy adults.
exclusion.E5: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses, only small-volume corrected results, or that used partial brain coverage, without an accompanying whole-brain map.
exclusion.E6: Studies that report only seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents) without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map. Peak coordinates originating from PPI, DCM, seed-selection, or mediation analyses are not whole-brain task activation coordinates and do not satisfy the whole-brain evidence criterion.
exclusion.E7: Studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., subgroup vs subgroup, patient vs control, gender differences)
